campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 15, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council agenda for September 15, 2026 includes a proposed update to the city's theater use policy, a cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose for a resurfacing project, and an annual update to the city's investment policy. The agenda also lists a budget adjustment to fund a replacement project.
keyTopics: Proposed modifications to Council Policy Section 14 (Theater Use Policy), effective September 16th
Cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose, not to exceed $335,000, for a resurfacing project
Annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27
Budget adjustment to fund replacement of remaining items

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council's September 16, 2026 agenda listed routine business, two final map approvals for lot splits, two appeals of Planning Commission decisions, and a discussion of law enforcement service options ahead of upcoming town hall meetings. The agenda also included approval of prior meeting minutes, vendor payment registers, and an update to the city's Conflict of Interest Code.
keyTopics: Final map approvals for lot splits at 20517 Carniel Avenue and 19351 Saratoga Los Gatos Road
Appeal of Planning Commission approval of a single-family residence and ADU design review/setback variance at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of Planning Commission approval of a three-lot subdivision (Tentative Map, Design Review, CEQA exemption) at 14486 Oak Place
Discussion of law enforcement service options ahead of September 19 and 30 town hall meetings
Resolution amending the City of Saratoga Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council agenda for September 22, 2026 includes a wastewater treatment plant agreement, a VTA Board appointment, a temporary moratorium on certain detention/custodial facility applications, commission appointments, and an updated legal services contract. The agenda also lists minutes approval from the prior meeting and a look-ahead council calendar tied to Housing Element implementation.
keyTopics: Resolution authorizing Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Reappointment of Councilmember Jonathan D. Weinberg to the VTA Board for two more years
Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on applications for detention or custodial facilities and custodial-processing facilities
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP, setting a $21,500 monthly retainer for up to 70 hours plus a $385 hourly rate

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 6, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's agenda for October 6, 2026, included routine business such as approving prior meeting minutes, accounts payable, and payroll reports. It also listed items on a contractor bid issue for tree services, a contract amendment, an updated Finance Commission work plan, a proposed update to the Town's purchasing policy, and a review of July 2026 financial reports.
keyTopics: Relieving Denali Tree Services of its bid due to a bidder's mistake
First Amendment to an agreement authorized for execution by the Town Manager
Finance Commission's updated 2026 Work Plan
Resolution amending the Town's Purchasing Policy (Policy 4-06)
July 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 30, 2026
san-jose.summary: This agenda covers routine administrative business for San José's Rules and Open Government Committee, including review of upcoming council meeting agendas and several special event approvals requiring use of city funds or facilities. It also lists multiple council member proposals on license plate reader data policies and council transparency rules around non-disclosure agreements.
keyTopics: Approval of 'Free Use' of the Janet Gray Hayes Rotunda for a Councilmember Mulcahy-sponsored event, 'Conversations for Good 2026: A Regenerative Future'
Approval of the District 9 End-of-Term, Farewell Celebration as a city council sponsored special event
Retroactive approval of the Golden State Valkyries flag raising event sponsored by the Mayor's office
Proposals on council transparency and private non-disclosure agreements (Ortiz, Campos, Cohen, Candelas, Casey)
Two separate proposals on automated license plate reader data access, internal controls, and safeguards

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee — September 29, 2026
mountain-view.summary: This Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee agenda covers the city's draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan and the 2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory. The meeting includes a public comment period and time for committee and staff discussion.
keyTopics: Draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan
2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council's agenda for October 6, 2026 includes recognitions for Little League All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week, along with routine approvals. Public hearings on the agenda cover new water conservation rules for nonfunctional turf, a proposed service worker retention ordinance, and public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.
keyTopics: Public hearing and introduction of an ordinance implementing AB 1572 to prohibit potable water use for irrigating nonfunctional turf, found exempt from CEQA under Guidelines Section 15307
Discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation

Amendment to a purchase agreement with WSP USA Inc. for environmental consulting at the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill, increasing the not-to-exceed amount to $385,000 and extending through October 2028
Authorization to negotiate and execute a PG&E easement deed over a portion of the Clean Water Facility

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 6, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council's agenda for October 6, 2026 includes closed-session items on potential litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue, a recognition of the Community Development Department, and a routine consent calendar covering minutes, treasurer's reports, and a retiree health insurance resolution. It also lists a property exchange agreement for the Finch property at $11.8 million, a public information session on a soil remediation plan at The Rise, and a TEFRA public hearing on conduit financing related to The Rise.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of the Community Development Department (Planning, Building, Housing, and Code Enforcement Divisions)
Resolution increasing employer PEMHCA medical insurance contributions for certain retired annuitants
Exchange agreement for the Finch property at a negotiated purchase price of $11.8 million
Public information session and TEFRA hearing on soil remediation and conduit financing for The Rise

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — September 22, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council's agenda for this meeting includes a public hearing on a proposed housing development at 451-475 El Camino Real, which would involve annexing the land into the city, rezoning it, and approving plans for 408 new homes. The agenda also lists closed-session discussions on existing and anticipated legal matters, including a case involving the city's power utility and the state's Department of Water Resources.
keyTopics: Public hearing on prezoning, land use designation, annexation, and a subdivision map to allow 408 residential units at 451-475 El Camino Real, with an Environmental Impact Report prepared under CEQA
Closed-session discussion on existing litigation: City of Santa Clara (Silicon Valley Power) and Northern California Power Agency vs. California Department of Water Resources
Closed-session discussion on anticipated litigation involving one potential case

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council's September 15, 2026 agenda listed several financial and infrastructure items, including a federal housing grant plan, red light camera traffic safety data, and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The agenda also included bond refunding actions tied to the former Redevelopment Agency's Successor Agency.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolutions related to the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency, including sale and issuance of refunding bonds

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — October 2, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee's agenda for this meeting lists staff and committee member comments, plus an update on long duration resiliency for the electric system. The agenda notes this item is classified as 'Not a Project' under CEQA review.
keyTopics: Update on Electric System Long Duration Resiliency
CEQA status determination of 'Not a Project' for the resiliency item
Staff comments
Committee member comments and announcements
